summary: In the aftermath of the battle, Tank drapes a sheet over his dead brother and the other bodies are covered. Morpheus lies covered with a cold sweat while the Agents break into his mind. Neo asks what is happening; Tank explains it is like hacking a computer, and that eventually Morpheus's mind will crack and his alpha pattern will shift from a chaotic to an ordered symmetrical pattern, at which point he will tell them anything. Tank reveals the Agents want the codes to Zion's mainframe that every ship's leader is given, which could let them destroy Zion. Trinity paces relentlessly; Tank insists Zion is more important than any of them. Trinity sees Cypher's dead body, rage overtakes her, and she kicks him, cursing. Neo insists there must be something they can do, and Tank declares they have to pull the plug. Trinity is shocked, asking if he means to kill Morpheus, and Tank replies they have no other choice.

what_changes.before: Unconscious but holding out, his mind resisting the Agents' intrusion
what_changes.after: Doomed to break, his alpha pattern set to change to an ordered symmetrical one after which he will reveal everything
what_changes.evidence: it will crack and his alpha pattern will change from this to this

what_changes.after: Consumed by rage at the sight of Cypher's body, lashing out physically
what_changes.evidence: Rage overtakes her and she kicks him. TRINITY Goddamnit! Goddamnit!

what_changes.before: Explaining the situation and the stakes to Neo and Trinity
what_changes.after: Committed to killing Morpheus to protect Zion, rejecting any alternative
what_changes.evidence: There is. We have to pull the plug. TANK Trinity, we don't have any other choice.

what_changes.before: Ignorant of what the Agents are doing and what they want
what_changes.after: Learns they are breaking into Morpheus's mind for Zion's mainframe codes
what_changes.evidence: The leader of every ship is given the codes to Zion's mainframe computer

event_hint.one_line: The survivors gather over their dead and a dying Morpheus, grappling with how to stop the Agents from extracting Zion's codes

objects_that_matter: the codes to Zion's mainframe computer
uncertain: Whether the decision to pull the plug is actually carried out in this scene
Whether Neo will propose an alternative before Morpheus is killed
Trinity's response to Tank's insistence that Zion is more important than Morpheus

minds.wants: To make the others accept that Morpheus must be killed to protect Zion.
minds.feels: Freshly gutted by his brother's death, he is channeling all his grief into a hard, protective duty — the only way he can keep from drowning is to become the one who makes the unbearable decision. Killing Morpheus costs him dearly; Morpheus is his captain too.
minds.shows: Clinical, explanatory calm about the 'hacking' of the mind, then flat resolve ('We have to pull the plug'). He keeps his voice on logic and stakes rather than letting the grief through.
minds.basis: He has just covered his dead brother Dozer (sc-143) and now covers the other bodies; he explains the alpha pattern dispassionately, insists 'Zion is more important than me. Or you, or even Morpheus,' and is the one who names pulling the plug, adding 'we don't have any other choice' as if trying to close a door on himself.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is still a novice who needs the horror explained plainly and will fall in line once he understands the stakes.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo's 'There has to be something that we can do' is not confusion but refusal — the beginning of the alternative Tank believes does not exist.

believes_about.belief: That killing Morpheus is a clean act of loyalty to the cause and that Morpheus would want it.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is the choice the coming rescue will retroactively reframe as premature surrender; Tank cannot yet imagine Morpheus surviving.

minds.wants: Some outlet for the dread of losing Morpheus — and, failing that, a target for her fury.
minds.feels: She is already bracing for Morpheus's death; the sight of Cypher's body — the traitor whose betrayal helped cause all this — gives her a sudden, usable rage that is easier to feel than the grief underneath.
minds.shows: Relentless pacing, then an explosive physical lash at the corpse ('Goddamnit! Goddamnit!'), then shock that turns Tank's euphemism into the raw word: 'You're going to kill him? Kill Morpheus?!'
minds.basis: In sc-143 she was the one who took Tank into her arms at the news of Dozer; here she paces instead of being comforted, redirects her emotion onto Cypher's body, and is the one who names the act as murder rather than 'pulling the plug.'

believes_about.belief: That his coldness about killing Morpheus means he doesn't care — that he has already given Morpheus up.
believes_about.wrong_because: His insistence that Zion outranks even Morpheus is a discipline he is imposing on himself, not an absence of love; he is protecting the crew from a choice that also destroys him.

believes_about.belief: That he deserves only contempt, that he is simply the cause of their ruin.
believes_about.wrong_because: Kicking a dead man does nothing but spend her fury; it cannot reach the living problem, and it lets her avoid the harder fear about Morpheus.

minds.wants: To refuse the terms of the choice — to find a third option where the others see only two.
minds.feels: A newcomer's horror at watching a man be tortured to betrayal, fused with a dawning, unearned certainty that he is not powerless here — the same instinct that will soon make him believe he can walk into a building full of Agents and bring Morpheus out.
minds.shows: He asks plain questions ('What are they doing to him?'), absorbs the explanation, then breaks the fatalism: 'There has to be something that we can do.'
minds.basis: He is the only one not yet hardened to the crew's triage logic; his question about the alpha pattern is genuine ignorance, and his refusal to accept 'pull the plug' is the first active expression of the belief that defines ev-026.

believes_about.belief: That Tank is giving up on Morpheus out of fear or coldness.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank is acting from grief and duty, not abandonment; Neo reads the resignation as cowardice because he cannot yet see the cost of the decision to the man making it.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus can still be saved — that his death is not inevitable.
believes_about.wrong_because: He has no plan yet and no skill; the belief is faith, not knowledge — which is exactly what will carry him into ev-026 and ev-028.

connects_back: Tank covering his brother's body follows directly from Dozer's death and Tank's charred wounds in sc-143.
Trinity's dread over Morpheus is the continuation of the capture that put him in the interrogation chair in sc-145.
The 'breaking into his mind' Tank describes is the on-screen torture by Smith and the serum in sc-145 made legible to the crew.
The stakes of Zion's codes are the reason the Agents took Morpheus alive rather than killing him in sc-145.
sets_up: Makes necessary the decision in ev-026 to attempt a rescue rather than pull the plug — Neo's refusal here is the seed of that choice.
Raises the urgency that drives Trinity to invoke her rank and join the assault in ev-026.
Establishes the countdown (Morpheus's mind cracking) that the rescue in ev-028 must beat.
Motivates the scale of armament Neo and Trinity gather in ev-026, given three Agents are guarding the building.
dramatic_function: It converts the off-screen torture into a moral deadline for the survivors, forcing each of them to reveal how they meet unbearable loss — Tank into duty, Trinity into rage, Neo into refusal — and in doing so it installs the ticking clock that makes the rescue not just desirable but necessary.
